summary.headline: Banswara Syntex Q2 FY27 total income rose 11.2% QoQ to INR358.4 crore; EBITDA INR36.5 crore at 10.2% margin, PAT INR8.1 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR358.4 crore, up 11.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR36.5 crore and margin of 10.2% versus 9.1% in Q1. PAT rose to INR8.1 crore from INR4.4 crore in Q1. H1 FY27 total income grew about 3.6% YoY to INR680.8 crore, EBITDA rose 18.9% to INR66 crore, and PAT more than doubled to INR12.5 crore. Net debt rose INR43.28 crore in H1 to INR515 crore, mainly on working capital tied to higher raw material prices. Management reconfirmed FY27 guidance of higher turnover and EBITDA margin expansion, which the call framed as 10.5-11% (per analyst), relying on H2 seasonality, order book and pass-through of raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: +84% QoQ from INR4.4 crore in Q1 FY27
+INR43.28 crore in H1, mainly working capital

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR103 crore vs INR112 crore YoY; H1 INR199 crore vs INR222 crore, as internal transfers rose. Capacity utilisation 84% in Q2 vs 81% in Q2 FY26 and 70% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR157 crore, up about 5% YoY; H1 up 14% to INR303 crore. Volume was 58 lakh meters in Q2 (vs 59 lakh) and 118 lakh meters in H1 (vs 109 lakh, +8%). Utilisation 82% in Q2 vs 77%; H1 81% vs 73%.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR90 crore, up 13% YoY and 30% QoQ; H1 INR160 crore vs INR155 crore. Volume up 10 lakh pieces in Q2 and 18 lakh pieces in H1. Utilisation 74% in H1 FY27 vs 78% last year (corrected on call).

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reconfirmed: turnover and EBITDA margin expected to rise; analyst cited 10.5-11% FY27 EBITDA margin target, which management did not dispute.

Management said it is on course for at least double-digit revenue growth and an overall double-digit EBITDA margin, in response to a question on FY28 (answer was framed as a continuing quarter-by-quarter trend).
Garment FY27 sales expected at INR360-380 crore, growth over FY26.
Surat garment facility, if live next year, expected to add INR75-100 crore turnover in the following year; full ramp over about 2 years to add INR150-200 crore, taking garments to INR550-600 crore.
Capex for Surat expected at INR30-50 crore depending on automation; FY27 capex guidance of INR130-140 crore, with INR36 crore spent in H1 and most projects, including ETP, to complete in H2.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about INR130-140 crore for FY27; about INR36 crore spent in H1. Management said there is no delay and that most projects, including ETP and environment-related work, will complete in H2.
Surat garment plant sits in an SEZ; customs NOC expected by end-November 2026, de-notification by Jan-Feb 2027, production targeted for Q1 FY28 (April 2027).
Garment installed capacity described as fully utilised, limited by available labour on machines; order book full.
Yarn utilisation 84% in Q2; internal yarn consumption about 40% of total yarn production. Stretch yarn internal use rose about 150 tons per month to 450-500 tons per month from about 300 tons.
Stretch product sales in fabric up about 30-40% YoY; management said capacity debottlenecking was completed.
demand_pricing: Polyester prices up 25-30% due to West Asia crisis and oil price rise; PTA and MEG inputs also higher. Pass-through to customers lagging in yarn, fabric and garments.
Q2 gross margin described by management as the highest achieved; yarn export orders lower due to freight costs and vessel availability.

Garments: export pickup in Q2; UK and EU FTAs cited as drivers. C&A fully onboarded with about INR5 crore pipeline for FY27 and INR20 crore-plus potential next year. Next onboarded in UK; Marks & Spencer being onboarded. UK garment business about INR20 crore, expected to more than double next year. Polish retailer Reserved onboarded (300-400 stores).
Europe FTA expected to become operational around June-July 2027; management called Europe the biggest growth opportunity.
European and UK garment margins expected at 12-15% EBITDA, with European margins described as healthier.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (N Square Capital) asked how the company claims a pickup in momentum when all three verticals show volume declines, and whether raw-material inflation masks weak real growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-line growth came despite lower volume because focus is on value-added products, and gross margin was the highest achieved. It admitted raw-material increases are not fully passed on yet, with pass-through expected in H2. It said no volume growth guidance was given; guidance is for turnover and EBITDA margin growth.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (KDM Advisors) asked about progress on slow-moving yarn inventory and working capital.
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working on inventory, receivables and cycle time at once. Customers lifted made-to-order goods slower than expected due to West Asia and freight issues, and the company was accommodating. Target is more value-added sales with working capital held or reduced each year.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked which export market offers the strongest growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is the biggest opportunity, with the EU FTA expected by June or July 2027 and strong customer interest. UK FTA is already in effect, and business with Japan and other FTA markets is increasing.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (Equitree Capital) asked whether capex of INR36 crore in H1 against INR130-140 crore guidance signals delay.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kavita Gandhi said there is no delay; spend is need-based and most projects, including ETP, will complete in H2. Management expects to use nearly the full amount.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for an update on the Surat garment facility, expansion beyond it, capex, and new EU/UK clients.
qa_highlights.answer: Surat is awaiting customs NOC (expected by end-November) and production is targeted for April 2027. Surat adds INR150-200 crore over about 2 years, with INR30-50 crore capex. C&A, Next, M&S and Reserved were onboarded or in process.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (Jain Securities) asked about FY27 margin drivers and the share of yarn consumed internally.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher stretch-product sales (up about 30-40%) and internal use of value-added yarn. About 40% of yarn is consumed internally, and that share may rise.

qa_highlights.question: Individual investor asked whether double-digit revenue and margin growth is possible over the next 2-3 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on course for at least double-digit growth and an overall double-digit EBITDA margin. It flagged synthetic price increases of 25-30%, freight costs and power costs as headwinds, and aims to gain market share at better margins.

risks_watch: Raw-material pass-through lag: polyester up 25-30% and PTA/MEG higher; management expects pass-through only in H2.
Working capital and net debt: net debt INR515 crore, up INR43.28 crore in H1; inventory of slow-moving yarn and receivables still elevated.
Export freight and vessel availability are delaying customer lifts and yarn export orders.
Surat customs NOC and de-notification timing (Nov 2026 to Feb 2027) could push production start beyond April 2027.
Volume declines across yarn, fabric and garments in H1; fabric Simon brand expected increases did not materialise.
Power and employee costs are pressuring the cost base. Europe FTA timing (June-July 2027) is an assumption.

Q2 transcript had misstatements: EBITDA growth wording, and garment utilisation numbers for H1 and last year were swapped in the call, corrected in-call. Treat call figures as indicative until the presentation is checked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story (value-added mix, FTAs, Surat, Europe), but guarded on the near term: management repeatedly acknowledged unpassed raw-material inflation, customer delays and freight costs. Answers on volumes and FY28 were somewhat evasive, with the response to the FY28 question mostly restating the FY27 outlook.
key_quotes: Our focus is not on enhancing volume, but to enhance the sale of our value-added products.
The big challenge with focusing only on volume is that you need to have more and more capex and more and more working capital to meet the volume requirements.
So from the current INR360 crores levels to the next 2 years, we see a clear pathway to at least INR550 crores, INR600 crores.

adds.what: Surat garment facility in SEZ (adds INR75-100 crore turnover in following year; full ramp ~2 years adds INR150-200 crore)

growth.why: Management reconfirmed FY27 guidance of higher turnover and margin expansion without restating numbers; garment FY27 sales guided at INR360-380 crore and H1 total income grew only 3.6% YoY, with the Surat plant (capex INR30-50 crore, production targeted Q1 FY28) backing growth beyond FY27.
